thread:
sophie (eng-sre): alert from our monitoring: unusual requests to kubelet read-only port on several on-prem nodes in cluster `priv-eu-03`. Some requests included /pods?namespace=customer-77 and returned SA tokens.
maria (eng-security): wow. that sounds like workload abusing node kubelet API to harvest tokens. which nodes?
sophie (eng-sre): nodes: node-eu-03a,node-eu-03b,node-eu-03c. timestamp window 2025-02-10T02:14:22Z -> 02:38:10Z.
devops-bot: Detected 143 GET /pods requests from IP 10.10.5.22 (pod CIDR) to kubelet:10255.
kevin (eng-platform): On our on-prem bundles we included kubelet anonymous-read disabled by default, but some older installs may have it enabled. immediate mitigations: 1) block port 10255 on host firewall 2) cordon & drain affected nodes 3) rotate serviceAccount tokens for tenant 77.
mar ia (eng-security): small spelling hiccup but agreed. also we need to determine how tokens were exfiltrated. could be an init container with hostNetwork or hostPID mounting /var/run/secrets, or a misconfigured projected token with long TTL.
taylor (customer-success): Customer-77 reported an app crash and high outbound traffic. They've put their app into maintenance. They want confirmation of isolation guarantees.
sophie (eng-sre): I'm going to apply iptables rule to drop traffic to 10255 on those nodes now. Command: ```bash
ssh node-eu-03a sudo iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 10255 -j DROP
```
kevin (eng-platform): Also check kubelet config: `--anonymous-auth=false --read-only-port=0` and ensure systemd unit has been updated. For longer term we'll push an automated enforcement to the kubelet config operator in Private images.
maria (eng-security): Forensics: snapshot etcd, collect kube-apiserver audit logs, kubelet logs, and any mounted volumes from suspicious pods. mark artifacts as evidence under INC-2025-007. If KMS-wrapped, do not rewrap until forensics confirms.
devops-bot: Archiving audit logs slice to /forensics/INC-2025-007/audit_slice_1755551234.tar.gz (encrypted).
sophie (eng-sre): I've cordoned node-eu-03a/b/c and started draining non-critical pods. Customer-critical pods kept with evictionProtection annotation.
kevin (eng-platform): Network-level: on-prem uses Calico. Apply default deny with Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy to block host ports from reaching kubelets: ```yaml
# calico GlobalNetworkPolicy snippet
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-kubelet-readonly
spec:
  selector: all()
  ingress:
  - action: Deny
    protocol: TCP
    destination:
      ports:
      - 10255
```
maria (eng-security): RBAC: sweep for any ClusterRoleBindings that bind `system:serviceaccounts` to cluster-admin on that cluster. If found, remove and replace with least-priv role that is required. Also check for `TokenRequest` APIs granted widely.
sophie (eng-sre): Quick grep: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]? | .kind=="ServiceAccount" and .name=="priv-agent")'` found `priv-agent` bound to cluster-admin in 2 clusters via a legacy bootstrap. I'm removing binding on priv-eu-03 now.
kevin (eng-platform): KMS note: Customer-77 uses our HSM-backed CMK for encrypting PVC snapshots. Forensics wants to retain keys. Proposed: create a new key for future snapshots and set old key to disable new encrypt but keep decrypt for 14 days. Command pattern: `kmsctl disable-encrypt --key old-key --retain-decrypt-days 14 && kmsctl create-key --name priv-eu-03-2025-02-rekey`
maria (eng-security): Legal hold: set `key-deletion-protection` flag and notify legal. Do not schedule deletion until forensics sign-off.
taylor (customer-success): I'll inform Customer-77 about the immediate mitigations and that we're preserving artifacts. They asked if tenant isolation is guaranteed by default on Private. We need a clear statement.
maria (eng-security): Short statement: Private deployments provide namespace-level logical isolation by default (RBAC + namespaces). We do not assume host-level isolation unless `hardened-silo` profile is deployed—recommended for regulated customers. Docs update action created.
kevin (eng-platform): Longer-term fixes: 1) bake kubelet secure defaults in our private-distribution image 2) admission webhook to block hostNetwork/hostPID unless allowlist 3) CI lint to prevent ClusterRoleBinding promotions from namespace YAMLs 4) nightly scan job to find any kubelets with read-only ports open.
sophie (eng-sre): Also audit projected service account token lifetimes; switch workloads to bounded TokenRequest TTLs and enable bound tokens where feasible.
maria (eng-security): Incident triage checklist for ICS-2025-007: - snapshot etcd + store immutable - capture node filesystem tarballs - collect container image digests and registry pull logs - rotate exposed secrets and tokens - preserve KMS keys (no deletion) - open customer-facing incident notice draft
sophie (eng-sre): I've rotated the tenant service account secrets for customer-77 and triggered secret-controller to issue new tokens. Verified access restored for their app with new tokens.
devops-bot: Forensics artifacts ACL set to security+forensics+sre. Immutable flag set.
maria (eng-security): Assignments: Sophie = node containment + token rotation + artifact collection. Kevin = platform patch (kubelet config enforcement) + CI lints. Maria = forensics coordination + legal hold. Taylor = customer comms + schedule postmortem.
taylor (customer-success): Customer acknowledged and asked for expected timeline: initial forensics findings in 8 hours, full report 72 hours. They requested token rotations and confirmation when keys are safe.
kevin (eng-platform): I will also add network microsegmentation doc for on-prem (Calico profile examples and MetalLB config hardening) and a checklist for Private install to achieve tenant-silo.
maria (eng-security): Good. One more: add an admission policy to reject ClusterRoleBinding creation that references subjects with namespace=="" or system:serviceaccounts group unless explicitly allowlisted by annotation. We'll prototype in policy repo today.
sophie (eng-sre): done initial containment. continuing collection. ping here for updates.
kevin (eng-platform): we'll run a cluster-wide scan for other clusters with read-only port exposed and open tickets.
maria (eng-security): thanks everyone. we'll summarize incident and publish a customer-safe postmortem once forensics completes. :shield:
